scenes.tts: Inside the cortex, why don't interneurons dive into the cortical plate at once?
scenes.visual: Title card: Staying in the Lane. Magenta dots entering the side of the cortex.
scenes.narration: Inside the cortex, why don't interneurons dive into the cortical plate at once?

scenes.tts: Picture the young cortical wall. Under the meninges, the brain's covering, lies the marginal zone. Below it is the cortical plate.
scenes.visual: A cortical-wall cross-section. Labels appear one at a time: meninges, marginal zone, cortical plate.
scenes.narration: Picture the young cortical wall. Under the meninges, the brain's covering, lies the marginal zone. Below it is the cortical plate.

scenes.tts: Deeper still are the intermediate zone and the subventricular zone.
scenes.visual: Labels: intermediate zone, subventricular zone, ventricle.
scenes.narration: Deeper still are the intermediate zone and the subventricular zone.

scenes.tts: Interneurons travel in two streams. One runs in the marginal zone, the other deep in the subventricular and lower intermediate zones.
scenes.visual: Two glowing lanes, top and bottom, filled with moving magenta dots. The plate between them holds few interneurons.
scenes.narration: Interneurons travel in two streams. One runs in the marginal zone, the other deep in the subventricular and lower intermediate zones.

scenes.tts: Both lanes are lined with a chemokine, a small secreted protein first known for steering immune cells.
scenes.visual: The lanes take on a soft glow of a signal molecule.
scenes.narration: Both lanes are lined with a chemokine, a small secreted protein first known for steering immune cells.

scenes.tts: It is called C X C L twelve. The meninges make it above. Dividing precursors of projection neurons make it below.
scenes.caption: It is called CXCL12. The meninges make it above. Dividing precursors of projection neurons make it below.
scenes.visual: Label CXCL12. Sources marked: meninges above, dividing precursors in the deep wall below.
scenes.narration: It is called CXCL12. The meninges make it above. Dividing precursors of projection neurons make it below.

scenes.tts: The interneurons carry its receptor, C X C R four.
scenes.caption: The interneurons carry its receptor, CXCR4.
scenes.visual: Zoom on one dot: receptors labelled CXCR4 on its surface.
scenes.narration: The interneurons carry its receptor, CXCR4.

scenes.tts: In a chamber assay, precursor cells moved toward C X C L twelve placed on one side.
scenes.caption: In a chamber assay, precursor cells moved toward CXCL12 placed on one side.
scenes.visual: Two-chamber animation: chemokine below; cells cross the membrane downward.
scenes.narration: In a chamber assay, precursor cells moved toward CXCL12 placed on one side.

scenes.tts: Spread evenly on both sides, it gave no extra crossing of the membrane.
scenes.visual: Chemokine equal above and below; crossing drops to baseline.
scenes.narration: Spread evenly on both sides, it gave no extra crossing of the membrane.

scenes.tts: In this assay, extra crossing needed a difference in concentration.
scenes.visual: Label: in this assay, they follow a difference.
scenes.narration: In this assay, extra crossing needed a difference in concentration.

scenes.tts: Now take the receptor away. Where do the interneurons end up?
scenes.visual: Wild-type and receptor-mutant walls side by side, the mutant's dots hidden.
scenes.narration: Now take the receptor away. Where do the interneurons end up?

scenes.tts: In two thousand eight, two groups blocked or deleted the receptor in mice.
scenes.caption: In 2008, two groups blocked or deleted the receptor in mice.
scenes.visual: Credits: López-Bendito, Marín and colleagues; Li, Pleasure, Rubenstein and colleagues, 2008.
scenes.narration: In 2008, two groups blocked or deleted the receptor in mice.

scenes.tts: The interneurons left their streams and entered the cortical plate early. And they spread less widely across the cortex.
scenes.visual: In the mutant, dots drop out of the lanes early and bunch near the side where they entered.
scenes.narration: The interneurons left their streams and entered the cortical plate early. And they spread less widely across the cortex.

scenes.tts: Many late-born cells that entered early ended up too deep, though not all did.
scenes.visual: Some late-born dots settle too deep; a few reach the upper layers.
scenes.narration: Many late-born cells that entered early ended up too deep, though not all did.

scenes.tts: Early entry and narrow spread can come from one defect, not two.
scenes.visual: Two labels, early entry and narrow spread, merge into one.
scenes.narration: Early entry and narrow spread can come from one defect, not two.

scenes.tts: If cells spent the same time in the lane, moving more slowly would narrow the spread, but they would not enter early.
scenes.visual: Toy model on screen: slower speed, same time in the lane. Spread shrinks; entry time unchanged.
scenes.narration: If cells spent the same time in the lane, moving more slowly would narrow the spread, but they would not enter early.

scenes.tts: If they leave the lane sooner, they spread less and enter early. That matches the mutants.
scenes.visual: Toy model: same speed, shorter time in the lane. Spread shrinks and entry comes early. Tick.
scenes.narration: If they leave the lane sooner, they spread less and enter early. That matches the mutants.

scenes.tts: Normal cells must leave too. Embryonic interneurons gathered near beads soaked in the chemokine.
scenes.visual: A bead soaked in CXCL12; embryonic interneurons cluster around it.
scenes.narration: Normal cells must leave too. Embryonic interneurons gathered near beads soaked in the chemokine.

scenes.tts: Interneurons from newborn mice did not.
scenes.visual: Newborn interneurons ignore the bead.
scenes.narration: Interneurons from newborn mice did not.

scenes.tts: So to leave a lane, a cell may stop answering the signal.
scenes.visual: A dot's receptors dim; it drifts out of the lane. Label: proposed.
scenes.narration: So to leave a lane, a cell may stop answering the signal.

scenes.tts: That compares ages, not single cells. It fits the idea but does not prove it.
scenes.visual: Embryonic and newborn cells side by side, labelled: different ages.
scenes.narration: That compares ages, not single cells. It fits the idea but does not prove it.

scenes.tts: The cortical plate also makes neuregulin three. It attracts interneurons that carry its receptor, erb B four.
scenes.caption: The cortical plate also makes Neuregulin-3. It attracts interneurons that carry its receptor, ErbB4.
scenes.visual: A solid pull arrow from the plate, labelled Nrg3, toward dots with ErbB4 receptors.
scenes.narration: The cortical plate also makes Neuregulin-3. It attracts interneurons that carry its receptor, ErbB4.

scenes.tts: How the two are coordinated is still being worked out.
scenes.visual: The dimming receptor and the pull arrow side by side, with an open question mark between them.
scenes.narration: How the two are coordinated is still being worked out.

scenes.tts: Then the cells turn into the plate, toward their layer.
scenes.visual: The dot turns radially and settles in a layer.
scenes.narration: Then the cells turn into the plate, toward their layer.

scenes.tts: Born outside the cortex, steered by what the cell can read. In the lanes, chemokine signalling helps hold a cell in place.
scenes.visual: Closing card with the full rule.
scenes.narration: Born outside the cortex, steered by what the cell can read. In the lanes, chemokine signalling helps hold a cell in place.
